question:
I am handing over a finished system to a client whose in-house team will keep developing it after delivery. Besides the program itself, what written material should I prepare for the client, for its end users and for my own organization, and for how long should it be retained?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
I have gathered all the SWEBOK passages I need. Here are the guidelines, grouped by audience, drawn entirely from what the SWEBOK passages contain.

---

## Documentation to Prepare at System Handover

### A. For the Client and Its Maintenance/Development Team

**1. Functional specifications (requirements documentation)**
When the client will own or have the right to modify the source code, provide full documentation of the functional specifications so the new team can understand what the system is supposed to do.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 48895c1d3102a8915751] [SWEBOK excerpt 138b0c77c0da8e454cc7]." — /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)*

**2. Software design documents**
Deliver the software design documentation — architecture, component diagrams, class and object diagrams, structure charts, interface description languages, entity-relationship diagrams, and other structural and behavioural notations — so the new team can understand the system's internal organisation.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 48895c1d3102a8915751] [SWEBOK excerpt 138b0c77c0da8e454cc7]." — same file as above)*

**3. Design rationale**
Document the major decisions taken during design, including [SWEBOK excerpt 3632f2289fc30a05af8b] analysed to select one approach and reject others. Without this, reasons obvious to the original team will be opaque [SWEBOK excerpt b3830eb477e40d395002].
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 7599a55dbdd51a176f9e] long-term maintainability." — /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Design Concerns, Documentation, and Modeling/Recording Design Rationale for System Maintainability.md)*

**4. The test suite and test results**
Hand over the test specifications and test results so the maintenance team can re-run the test suite when they make changes and have evidence of the system's verified behaviour at the point of delivery.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 48895c1d3102a8915751] [SWEBOK excerpt 138b0c77c0da8e454cc7]." — Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)*

**5. Necessary operating environment description**
Provide documentation of the environment required to build, run, and maintain the software, including the software engineering tools used and any platform requirements.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 48895c1d3102a8915751] [SWEBOK excerpt 138b0c77c0da8e454cc7]." — Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)*

**6. Software Configuration Management (SCM) items and their documentation**
Hand over all configuration items as controlled artefacts: [SWEBOK excerpt c437c5c0efc61fcc52ed].
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt ae8c53959623d22d6586]." — /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management and Change Control/Software Configuration Items Selection and Change Recording.md)*

**7. Release notes, installation/upgrade instructions, and version description document (VDD)**
The release package should include release notes describing new capabilities, known problems, and platform requirements; installation or upgrade instructions; and a version description document (VDD) that records the physical contents of the release.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt ba2c3ad4c64b26bf5daf] [SWEBOK excerpt a957ee5cf5dffb6fa8dd])." — /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Release Management Tools and Documentation Requirements.md and /Software Release Management and Deployment Processes.md)*

**8. Software maintenance plan**
Prepare a maintenance plan during software development that specifies [SWEBOK excerpt c3f9b85a22b5819ebd7b], the scope of maintenance, the adaptation of maintenance processes and tools, and the maintenance organisation.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt dcd77385d2336dc761c2]." — /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Software Maintenance_ Organization, Configuration, and Quality/Software Maintenance Planning and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance Planning and Cost Estimation.md)*

**9. Operations and maintenance plan**
An operations and maintenance plan should be developed to cover the scope of operations and software maintenance, the adaptation of operations processes and tools, the identification of the operations organisation, and the estimate of operations and maintenance costs.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt e167e3ef9c825c28308c]… [SWEBOK excerpt e01e93edb1ea2b42bca7]." — /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Operations Plan and Supplier Management.md)*

---

### B. For End Users

**10. Information needed to determine whether the software meets user needs**
Provide users with documentation that allows them to judge whether the software is likely to meet their needs before or during use.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt cc579910ceea067b7451]" — Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)*

**11. Description of safe and unsafe use**
Document what constitutes safe and unsafe use of the software, as well as warnings of undesirable or dangerous consequences from use or misuse.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 61cf7d5a76e60fd95d85]… [SWEBOK excerpt 03093f1055a52d120f04]" — Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)*

**12. Guidance on protecting sensitive information**
Include an [SWEBOK excerpt 0d45389c08edc01f9a01].
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt cdf19b1e62ffd9c64fa3]" — Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)*

**13. Clear identification of warnings and critical procedures**
User documentation must clearly identify warnings and critical procedures, particularly for installation, operation, administration, and other functions performed by various user groups.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 571f0df8c769bcf13a65]." — Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)*

**14. User manuals and other written products**
Produce the [SWEBOK excerpt fa042d0e8c44843f59d4] — which may include user manuals, technical reports, diagrams, and charts — and ensure they are [SWEBOK excerpt 1515fcd9fd348b2ae15b].
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt df869b45c84fc60eb41e]… [SWEBOK excerpt 87d24b3ff080e464a7e7]." — /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Collaboration, Communication, and Cognition in Software Engineering/Writing and Communication in Software Engineering.md)*

---

### C. For the Delivering Organisation (Internal Records)

**15. Requirements specifications, design documents, tool details, test specifications, and adopted methods**
The delivering organisation should retain, for its own future reference, the [SWEBOK excerpt 75c7ba3d6407f006d4af].
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt dc2237a7b6da15a1fa6a]" — Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)*

**16. Record of problems encountered during development**
Document problems encountered during the development process so that the organisation can learn from them and avoid recurrence on future projects.
*(source: "Problems encountered during the development process" — Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)*

**17. Lessons learned and measurement data**
At project closure, update the organisation's measurement database with relevant project data, undertake a retrospective analysis of issues, problems, risks, and opportunities encountered, and feed lessons learned into organisational learning and improvement endeavours.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt f5303d9f5a98d2a3cd10]… [SWEBOK excerpt 560298b5377d29b68977] endeavours." — /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Measurement and Organizational Learning/Software Engineering Measurement and Organizational Learning.md)*

**18. Closure documentation including stakeholder acceptance and known problems**
Produce closure documentation that records relevant stakeholders' acceptance of the delivered system; any known problems at the point of closure should also be documented.
*(source: "Closure [SWEBOK excerpt 43fd4cd61e6b9cb5da09]." — /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Measurement and Organizational Learning/Project Closure and Archival Procedures.md)*

---

### D. Retention

**19. Retain documents for at least the product's life cycle, or as long as required by regulatory obligations**
All documentation [SWEBOK excerpt fa987ee347a46eae3c11] for the time required by relevant organisational or regulatory requirements — whichever is longer.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 3195bf83cb2eca8378f7]." — Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)*

**20. Archive project materials according to stakeholder-agreed rules, including method, location, duration, and destruction procedures**
After closure, [SWEBOK excerpt d038afb563d85e5d6ced] covering archival method, location, and duration, and those rules may also include destruction of sensitive information and the physical media on which copies reside.
*(source: "[SWEBOK excerpt f9addc8db2ee15e26b56]." — /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Measurement and Organizational Learning/Project Closure and Archival Procedures.md)*

---

**A note on what the SWEBOK does not cover here:** The passages retrieved do not specify distinct retention periods for different document types (e.g., "requirements for 7 years, test results for 3 years"). The only retention rule stated is the one in guideline 19 above. For more granular retention schedules you would need to consult applicable regulatory or contractual frameworks outside the SWEBOK.
